page: Microsoft Azure D2ls_v5 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the DLSv5 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8370C core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. The server is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance but poor multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1889.98, and the Geekbench single-core score is 1589.0, both representing average tier performance. However, multi-core benchmarks show limitations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1932.38 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1861.0, both falling into the bottom 10% category. Memory performance is also constrained, with uncached read and write large-block bandwidths measured at 14.32 GB/sec and 13.3 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2ls_v5 offers a low-resource, dedicated-CPU entry point without the overhead of local storage or high memory capacities. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective option for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have minimal memory footprints. Suitable workloads include lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, static web serving, and small-scale development or testing environments. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
